Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate—For the Plaintiff-Appellants.

Ruhul Amin and others ------Plaintiff-Appellants
VS
Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) & others ------ Defendant- Respondents
full_judgment: 3. It is the plaint case that Nawab Sir Salimullah was the owner of the suit property along with other property, died, leaving eldest son, Nawab Habibullah Bahadur, who became owner of the suit property by inheritance, made heba-bil-ewaj of the suit property along with other land on taking Quran Sharif and a Diamond Ring, to his wife, Ayesha Begum by registered heba-bil-ewaj deed No. 1070 dated 30-3-1939. While Ayesha Begum was in possession of the aforesaid land by saf kabala deed No. 690 dated 17-2-1940 transferred the said land to Most. Sufia Begum. Sufia Begum transferred 0.33 acres of land to his heirs, daughter, Syeda Jahura Begum by kabala deed No. 4546 registered on 1-1-1968. Jahura Begum by heba-bil-ewaj deed No. 3334 dated 12-7-1984 transferred 0.2805 acres of land to his brother, Syed Reaz Selim, who by saf kabala deed 375 dated 22-8-1984 transferred 0.1053 acres of land to one Feroza Haider. On the remaining land by constructing pucca construction, after paying rent regularly to the Government and holding No. 1/e/3 Shahbagh road was opened by Dhaka City Corporation and he also took all the connection relating enjoyment of the suit property and Amir Hossain was stationed in the suit premises as caretaker and having need of money, by saf kabala deed No. 148 dated 17-1-1990 transferred 0.1752 acres of land to Moin Uddin and delivered possession who mutated his name and paying all other required taxes to the Government and its different department. Mainuddin by saf kabala deed No. 4446 dated 1-9-2005 transferred 0.09 acres of land to plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and by kabala deed No. 4447 of the same date transferred 0.0852 acres of land to plaintiff Nos. 4-5 and delivered possession. All the plaintiffs are enjoying the suit land and while they are in peaceful possession, through their caretaker Amir Hossain, came to know on 25-10-2007 that some employees of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical College, (BSMMU) along with some other person of District Administration are measuring the suit property and having come to know of the aforesaid facts, plaintiffs went to the office of defendant No. 2 and on query came to know that the property has been acquired by the Government for requiring body, BSMMU. Plaintiffs wanted to know when land was acquired for the aforesaid University defendant No. 2 asked plaintiff to meet him in his office on 26-10-2007. Plaintiffs went to the said office where from came to know that the suit land was acquired in LA Case No. 2/78-79. Plaintiff wanted to see the file but defendant declined and some photo copies of LA Case No. 2/78-79 was given to the plaintiffs. From defendant No. 2 plaintiffs further came to know that one Shuktara Printers Company Ltd filed Title Suit No. 224 of 2004 against the acquisition proceeding where all the papers of land acquisition case No. 2/78-79 were submitted. Plain-tiffs went to the learned Advocate, Md Khalilur Rahman, lawyer for the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 224 of 2004 and from him, plaintiffs could know that predecessor of defendant No. 1, IPGMR applied to the Government for acquisition and requisition and 5 acres of land was acquired by the Government but IPGMR having no fund and informed it has Taka 45,00,000 (forty five lacks) only, which the defendant No. 1 was able to contribute at the relevant time and only the land covered by the said money may be acquired and as per said price, per decimals of land at the relevant time, was at taka 4,43,574 and accordingly an area of 1.03 acres of land was acquired and which was delivered to defendant No. 1 who having got possession, constructed pucca boundary wall upon said land where 3rd/4th class employees of defendant No. 1 are now staying. The suit land is far way from the aforesaid 1.333 acres of land and there are some old structure in between the acquired land and the suit land. Defendant No. 1 wanted to acquire more land and applied to the Government and the Government final measure those land and sketch map was prepared and the suit land was out side the said sketch map. Defendant No. 1 in connivance with defendant No. 2 tried to increase the land by acquiring 2.04 acres of land and after that, no notice has been issued and no compensation money was paid. It is further stated that Emergency Requisition of Property Act of 1948 has longevity of 34 years which expired in 1982 and thereafter, on the basis of the said law, no requisition should be made. It is further stated that in the plaint it is stated that Shuktara Printers was given false notice against which it filed that suit and the suit is still pending with injunction granted by the High Court Division. Along with plaint, plaintiff attached a sketch map showing position of the suit land.
